mgmt_bio.text: He graduated cum laude from Ateneo de Manila University with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Economics and received his MBA from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania. He worked for Philippine Investment Management Consultants (PHINMA) in Manila and for Bancom International and American Express Bank in Hong Kong, then founded First Pacific in May 1981, the Hong Kong-based investment management and holding company where he serves as managing director and chief executive officer. He became president and chief executive officer of Manila Electric Company (Meralco) effective 1 June 2023, and Meralco identifies him as its chairman and CEO.

sentences.text: Manuel Velez Pangilinan remains chairman and chief executive, while Ronnie L. Aperocho serves as executive vice-president and chief operating officer, overseeing day-to-day operations.
Bernido H. Liu has been an independent director since June 30, 2026 and chairs the audit committee.

Pangilinan attributed the record 2025 result to steady distribution and generation growth plus a "balanced mix of regulated and unregulated operations", with core net income up 14 percent to P50.6 billion, and in July 2026 said full-year earnings should be ahead of 2025 on higher demand.

sentences.quote: "All of these realities point us in one direction: Meralco must evolve," Aperocho said.

citations.title: Manila Electric Company (PSE:MER) Transcript:

sentences.text: Meralco is the Philippines' largest private distribution utility, serving more than 8.2 million customers in Metro Manila and nearby provinces, and its distribution business supplied 58 percent of 2025 earnings.
Generation is the main growth engine: MGEN expects to add 1,731 MW to its 5,069-MW portfolio to reach 6,800 MW, and targets more than 10,000 MW by 2030.
The P200-billion MTerra Solar Phase 1, with 1,373 MW of solar and 825 MW of battery storage, is inaugurated and ready to serve a 600 MW supply agreement with Meralco.
Earnings have compounded, with core net income up 14 percent to a record P50.6 billion in 2025 and first-half 2026 core income of P26.5 billion.

sentences.quote: Regulatory risks and tariff reset delays remain, but strong financial flexibility and major investments in renewables and storage support positive outlook.
sentences.text: Key risks include regulatory uncertainty and tariff reset delays plus weather-sensitive demand.
